title: Joshua Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 22.

questions.question: Who did Joshua call at the beginning of Joshua Chapter 22?
options: The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh
The Levites and the priests
The children of Judah and Simeon
The elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Joshua called the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh as stated in Joshua 22:1.

questions.question: What did Joshua commend the tribes for doing according to Joshua 22:2?
options: Keeping all that Moses commanded and obeying Joshua's voice
Building an altar on the other side of Jordan
Defeating their enemies alone
Gathering riches and cattle
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping all that Moses commanded and obeying Joshua's voice
questions.explanation: Joshua praised them for keeping all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded and for obeying his voice as found in Joshua 22:2.

questions.question: True or False: The tribes had left their brethren many days before Joshua gave his speech.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:3 states that they had not left their brethren these many days unto this day, so the statement is false.

questions.question: According to Joshua 22:4, what had the LORD given unto the brethren?
options: Rest as He promised them
Victory over all nations
A new tabernacle
A great altar to build
questions.correctAnswer: Rest as He promised them
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:4 says the LORD had given rest unto the brethren as He promised them.

questions.question: What did Joshua instruct the tribes to do in Joshua 22:5?
options: Take diligent heed to do the commandment and law, love the LORD, walk in His ways, keep His commandments, cleave to Him, and serve Him with all heart and soul
Build an altar by the Jordan
Divide the spoil of their enemies
Gather riches and cattle
questions.correctAnswer: Take diligent heed to do the commandment and law, love the LORD, walk in His ways, keep His commandments, cleave to Him, and serve Him with all heart and soul
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:5 commands them to diligently follow the law, love the LORD, and serve Him with all their heart and soul.

questions.question: What did Joshua do before sending the tribes away in Joshua 22:6?
options: Blessed them
Gave them silver and gold
Built an altar
Sent priests with them
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed them
questions.explanation: Joshua blessed them before sending them away, as stated in Joshua 22:6.

questions.question: Where had Moses given possession to one half of the tribe of Manasseh?
options: Bashan
Gilead
Canaan
Shiloh
questions.correctAnswer: Bashan
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:7 states Moses gave possession to one half of Manasseh in Bashan.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua encouraged the tribes to return with much riches including cattle, silver, gold, brass, iron, and raiment.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:8 instructs them to return with much riches and various spoils including cattle and metals.

questions.question: From which place did the children of Reuben, Gad, and half tribe of Manasseh depart to go to their land of possession?
options: Shiloh
Jerusalem
Bashan
Gilgal
questions.correctAnswer: Shiloh
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:9 states they departed from Shiloh in the land of Canaan.

questions.question: What significant structure did the tribes build by the Jordan when they reached the borders of Canaan?
options: A great altar to see to
A fortress
A well
A tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: A great altar to see to
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:10 says they built a great altar by Jordan that was visible.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Israel immediately rejoiced when they heard about the altar built by the other tribes.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:12 shows that the whole congregation gathered to go to war, indicating they were upset, not rejoicing.

questions.question: Who did the children of Israel send to speak to the tribes about the altar?
options: Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest
Joshua himself
Moses
Caleb
questions.correctAnswer: Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:13 states they sent Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest.

questions.question: How many princes accompanied Phinehas to speak with the tribes?
options: Ten princes
Five princes
Twelve princes
Twenty princes
questions.correctAnswer: Ten princes
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:14 mentions that Phinehas was sent with ten princes from the tribes of Israel.

questions.question: In Joshua 22, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: To love the LORD your God and walk in all His ways
To build an altar by the Jordan
To divide the spoil of enemies
To gather riches and cattle
questions.correctAnswer: To love the LORD your God and walk in all His ways
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:5 instructs to love the LORD and walk in His ways before the instructions about building altars or dividing spoils.

questions.question: True or False: The altar built by the tribes was hidden and hard to see.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:10 says they built a great altar to see to, meaning it was very visible, so the statement is false.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who was sent along with ten princes to speak to the children of Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh about the altar they built?
options: Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest
Joshua the son of Nun
Moses the servant of the LORD
Eleazar the high priest
questions.correctAnswer: Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:13 states that Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest was sent with ten princes to the children of Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh to address the issue of the altar they built.

questions.question: What was the role of the ten princes who accompanied Phinehas to the land of Gilead?
options: Each was a chief house prince and head of their father's house among the thousands of Israel
They were priests assisting Phinehas in sacrifices
They were spies sent to gather intelligence
They were warriors preparing for battle
questions.correctAnswer: Each was a chief house prince and head of their father's house among the thousands of Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:14 describes the ten princes as each being a chief house prince and head of their fathers' houses among the thousands of Israel, highlighting their leadership and authority.

questions.question: What was the primary accusation the whole congregation of Israel made against the children of Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh regarding the altar they built?
options: That they had turned away from following the LORD and rebelled by building the altar
That they stole possessions from other tribes
That they refused to fight in the battle
That they had worshipped foreign gods
questions.correctAnswer: That they had turned away from following the LORD and rebelled by building the altar
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:16 records the accusation that by building the altar, the children of Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh had turned away from the LORD and were in rebellion against Him and Israel.

questions.question: According to the leaders of Israel, what past iniquity was mentioned as a warning against rebellion and building an altar apart from the LORD?
options: The iniquity of Peor
The sin of Achan
The rebellion of Korah
The worship of the golden calf
questions.correctAnswer: The iniquity of Peor
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:17 references the iniquity of Peor as a past sin from which Israel was not cleansed until that day, warning against turning away from following the LORD and rebelling again by building an altar.

questions.question: What consequence did the congregation of Israel fear would happen if the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh rebelled by building the altar?
options: That the LORD would be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel
That the altar would be destroyed by fire
That the cities of Israel would be invaded
That the priests would refuse to minister
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD would be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:18 states the fear that if the altar was built in rebellion, the LORD would be angry with the entire congregation of Israel, indicating the seriousness of unity and obedience in worship.

questions.question: What did the leaders suggest the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh do if their land was unclean?
options: Pass over to the land where the LORD's tabernacle dwells and take possession among them
Cleanse their land with sacrifices
Destroy the altar they built
Offer peace offerings to atone
questions.correctAnswer: Pass over to the land where the LORD's tabernacle dwells and take possession among them
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:19 advises that if their land was unclean, they should cross over to the land of the LORD’s possession where His tabernacle was and take possession among the other tribes, rather than rebel by building an altar beside the LORD’s altar.

questions.question: Which individual’s sin is cited as an example of how one person’s trespass affected the whole congregation of Israel?
options: Achan the son of Zerah
Phinehas the son of Eleazar
Moses the servant of the LORD
Joshua the son of Nun
questions.correctAnswer: Achan the son of Zerah
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:20 reminds the Israelites of Achan’s sin in taking an accursed thing which brought wrath on all Israel, illustrating how individual rebellion impacts the whole community.

questions.question: How did the children of Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh respond to the accusation of rebellion?
options: They declared that the LORD knows if they are in rebellion or transgression and to save them if they are not
They admitted their guilt and repented
They refused to answer
They threatened to fight the rest of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They declared that the LORD knows if they are in rebellion or transgression and to save them if they are not
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:22 shows their confident reply that only the LORD knows if they have rebelled or transgressed, and they asked God not to save them falsely if they were innocent.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh admitted to building the altar to offer burnt offerings and sacrifices on it.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:23-29 clearly states that the altar was not built to offer burnt offerings, meat offerings, or peace offerings, but as a witness between the tribes to prevent future division.

questions.question: What was the intended purpose of the altar built by the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, according to their explanation?
options: To serve as a witness between them and the other tribes and their generations after them
To replace the altar at the LORD’s tabernacle
To offer sacrifices for their sins
To celebrate their military victories
questions.correctAnswer: To serve as a witness between them and the other tribes and their generations after them
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:26-28 explains that the altar was built to be a witness and a sign between the tribes so that future generations would know they all belong to the LORD and worship Him together.

questions.question: How does Joshua 22 teach about the importance of unity and communication among believers?
options: By showing how misunderstanding about the altar nearly caused conflict but was resolved by dialogue and explanation
By encouraging separate altars for each tribe
By advocating for isolation of different groups
By instructing to ignore accusations
questions.correctAnswer: By showing how misunderstanding about the altar nearly caused conflict but was resolved by dialogue and explanation
questions.explanation: The chapter narrates how the altar caused suspicion leading to a potential war (Joshua 22:11-12), but through communication and explanation (Joshua 22:21-29), peace and unity were restored, teaching believers to seek understanding.

questions.question: What does Joshua 22:18 suggest will happen if the people rebel against the LORD by building the altar?
options: The LORD will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel
They will immediately be blessed
Their enemies will flee
They will receive new land
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:18 warns that rebellion by building the altar will provoke the LORD's wrath not only on the builders but on the entire congregation, showing the communal consequences of disobedience.

questions.question: True or False: Phinehas and the princes were pleased with the explanation given by the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh about the altar.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:30 states that when Phinehas and the leaders heard the explanation, it pleased them, indicating their acceptance and relief that no rebellion had occurred.

questions.question: What did Phinehas say indicated that the LORD was among the people, according to Joshua 22:31?
options: That the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh had not committed trespass against the LORD
That the altar was destroyed by fire
That the LORD gave them victory in battle
That the people gathered for war
questions.correctAnswer: That the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh had not committed trespass against the LORD
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:31 explains Phinehas's assurance that the LORD was among them because the tribes in question had not rebelled or trespassed, showing God's presence is linked to obedience and unity.

questions.question: After understanding the situation about the altar, what was the reaction of the children of Israel towards the children of Reuben and Gad?
options: They blessed God and did not intend to go to war against them
They prepared for battle immediately
They demanded the altar be destroyed
They exiled them from the land
questions.correctAnswer: They blessed God and did not intend to go to war against them
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:33 states that after hearing the explanation, the children of Israel were pleased, blessed God, and had no intention to wage war against the tribes of Reuben and Gad.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 22.

questions.question: What reason did the children of Reuben and Gad give for building the altar by the Jordan?
options: To offer sacrifices apart from the LORD's altar
To serve as a witness between them and the other tribes
To rebel against the congregation of Israel
To establish a new place for burnt offerings
questions.correctAnswer: To serve as a witness between them and the other tribes
questions.explanation: They built the altar not for burnt offerings but as a witness between them and the other tribes, so future generations would acknowledge their shared faith (Joshua 22:26-28).

questions.question: According to Joshua 22, what did the LORD establish as a border between the children of Reuben and Gad and the other tribes?
options: The Dead Sea
The Jordan River
The Red Sea
Mount Sinai
questions.correctAnswer: The Jordan River
questions.explanation: The LORD made the Jordan River a border between the children of Reuben and Gad and the other tribes to separate their territories (Joshua 22:25).

questions.question: What was the reaction of Phinehas and the princes upon hearing the explanation from the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh about the altar?
options: They were angry and prepared for war
They were pleased and acknowledged the LORD was among them
They ignored the explanation and returned silently
They accused them of rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: They were pleased and acknowledged the LORD was among them
questions.explanation: Phinehas and the princes were pleased because the altar was not built to rebel against the LORD, showing the LORD's presence among them (Joshua 22:30-31).

questions.question: What name did the children of Reuben and Gad give to the altar they built, and what does it signify?
options: Ebal, meaning 'curse'
Ed, meaning 'witness'
Gilgal, meaning 'circle'
Mizpah, meaning 'watchtower'
questions.correctAnswer: Ed, meaning 'witness'
questions.explanation: They called the altar Ed as it was to be a witness between them that the LORD is God (Joshua 22:34).

questions.question: What was the concern of the other tribes about the altar built by the eastern tribes?
options: That it would be used to offer sacrifices in rebellion against the LORD
That it would obstruct the Jordan River
That it was made of improper materials
That it would cause division with neighboring nations
questions.correctAnswer: That it would be used to offer sacrifices in rebellion against the LORD
questions.explanation: The other tribes feared the altar represented rebellion and a turning away from the LORD by offering sacrifices apart from the LORD’s tabernacle (Joshua 22:16-19).

questions.question: Which historical event was referenced by the children of Israel as a warning against rebellion after the altar's construction?
options: The destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
Achan's trespass and the resulting wrath on Israel
The crossing of the Red Sea
The golden calf incident
questions.correctAnswer: Achan's trespass and the resulting wrath on Israel
questions.explanation: The children of Israel reminded them of Achan's sin which brought wrath upon the whole congregation, warning against rebellion (Joshua 22:20).

questions.question: What did the children of Reuben, Gad, and half-tribe of Manasseh swear regarding the altar's use?
options: They would offer burnt offerings there regularly
They would not rebel or offer sacrifices on that altar
They would make it the new center of worship
They would invite all tribes to worship there
questions.correctAnswer: They would not rebel or offer sacrifices on that altar
questions.explanation: They declared the altar was not for burnt offerings or sacrifices and that they would not rebel against the LORD (Joshua 22:29).

questions.question: True or False: The altar built by the eastern tribes was intended to replace the altar of the LORD before his tabernacle.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: They explicitly stated the altar was not for burnt offerings or sacrifices and was not meant to replace the LORD's altar (Joshua 22:29).

questions.question: True or False: The LORD's presence was confirmed among the tribes after the explanation about the altar was accepted.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Phinehas declared the LORD was among them since no trespass was committed, confirming His presence (Joshua 22:31).

questions.question: Which cross-biblical passage echoes the theme of unity and shared worship seen in Joshua 22 when addressing the altar dispute?
options: Deuteronomy 12:5-7
Exodus 20:3
1 Kings 18:21
Psalm 23
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 12:5-7
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 12:5-7 emphasizes centralized worship in the place the LORD chooses, paralleling the concern about altar worship in Joshua 22 and the importance of unified worship.

questions.question: How does the altar in Joshua 22 serve as an example of the biblical literary device known as 'inclusio'?
options: It frames the chapter by beginning and ending with the altar's purpose
It uses repetition of the word 'altar' throughout
It presents the altar as a metaphor for salvation
It contrasts two opposing tribes
questions.correctAnswer: It frames the chapter by beginning and ending with the altar's purpose
questions.explanation: The altar is introduced as a witness early and the chapter closes with its naming and purpose, creating an inclusio framing the narrative around this theme (Joshua 22:10, 22:34).

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word translated as 'witness' (Ed) in the context of the altar built by the eastern tribes?
options: It signifies a legal testimony or covenant reminder
It means 'sacrifice' or 'offering'
It denotes a place of refuge
It translates as 'peace' or 'reconciliation'
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies a legal testimony or covenant reminder
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Ed' means witness or testimony, emphasizing the altar's role as a covenantal reminder between tribes (Joshua 22:34).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of unity and shared faith present in Joshua 22's altar story?
options: Ephesians 4:3-6
Romans 12:2
Hebrews 11:1
James 2:14
questions.correctAnswer: Ephesians 4:3-6
questions.explanation: Ephesians 4:3-6 emphasizes unity of the Spirit and one faith, reflecting the importance of shared worship and covenant unity seen in Joshua 22.

questions.question: What does the building of the altar by the eastern tribes foreshadow in Israelite history?
options: The division of the kingdom into Israel and Judah
The destruction of the temple by Babylon
The establishment of synagogues
The exile in Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The division of the kingdom into Israel and Judah
questions.explanation: The altar symbolized a separation in worship practices and territory, foreshadowing later political and religious divisions like the split of Israel and Judah.

questions.question: How does the altar incident in Joshua 22 relate to the commandment against idolatry in Exodus 20:3-5?
options: The altar was a direct violation of the commandment
The altar was not for idols but a witness, so it did not violate the commandment
The altar was dedicated to Baal
The altar replaced the LORD's tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: The altar was not for idols but a witness, so it did not violate the commandment
questions.explanation: Though initially feared as rebellion, the altar was not for idol worship but served to affirm faithfulness to the LORD, aligning with the commandment (Joshua 22:29).

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific command does Joshua emphasize to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh before sending them back to their land?
options: To love the LORD their God and keep His commandments with all their heart and soul
To build an altar as a witness between the tribes
To wage war against their enemies until the land is fully possessed
To send offerings to the tabernacle regularly
questions.correctAnswer: To love the LORD their God and keep His commandments with all their heart and soul
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:5 commands the tribes to take diligent heed to do the law given by Moses, to love the LORD their God, walk in His ways, keep His commandments, cleave to Him, and serve Him wholeheartedly.

questions.question: According to Joshua 22:10, what significant action did the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh take at the Jordan border?
options: They built a large altar to be seen
They destroyed the cities of the Canaanites
They set up a tabernacle for worship
They crossed the Jordan to fight the enemy
questions.correctAnswer: They built a large altar to be seen
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:10 states that these tribes built a great altar by the Jordan, which was visible and notable ('to see to'), causing concern among the rest of Israel.

questions.question: What was the initial reaction of the rest of the Israelites upon hearing that the tribes built an altar by the Jordan?
options: They gathered at Shiloh to prepare for war against them
They sent a delegation to congratulate them
They ignored it, considering it insignificant
They joined them in building the altar
questions.correctAnswer: They gathered at Shiloh to prepare for war against them
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:12 reveals that the children of Israel assembled at Shiloh intending to go to war against the tribes, suspecting rebellion due to the altar.

questions.question: What theological concern did the Israelites express in accusing the tribes of building the altar?
options: That they were turning away from the LORD and rebelling by building a rival altar
That they were stealing land from other tribes
That they were refusing to pay tithes to the tabernacle
That they were inviting foreign gods into the camp
questions.correctAnswer: That they were turning away from the LORD and rebelling by building a rival altar
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:16 explicitly states the accusation that building the altar was a trespass against God, turning away from following the LORD and rebelling on that day.

questions.question: Which past sin is referenced in Joshua 22:17 as a cautionary example of iniquity affecting the whole congregation?
options: The sin of Peor
The worship of Baal
The idolatry of Jeroboam
The rebellion of Korah
questions.correctAnswer: The sin of Peor
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:17 mentions the iniquity of Peor, a sin associated with Moabite idolatry and immorality that brought a plague upon Israel, showing communal consequences of sin.

questions.question: What alternative did the Israelites offer if the altar-building tribes' land was unclean?
options: To pass over to the LORD’s possession where the tabernacle dwells and take possession among them
To build a tabernacle on their side of the Jordan
To offer sacrifices only at the new altar
To abandon their land and live with other tribes
questions.correctAnswer: To pass over to the LORD’s possession where the tabernacle dwells and take possession among them
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:19 proposes that if their land is unclean, they should join the LORD’s possession where His tabernacle is and take possession among the other tribes, rather than build a separate altar.

questions.question: What doctrinal principle about corporate sin and individual responsibility is illustrated by the reference to Achan in Joshua 22:20?
options: That one person’s sin can bring judgment on the entire community
That individual sins are isolated and do not affect others
That only priests are held accountable for sin
That sins of ancestors do not affect descendants
questions.correctAnswer: That one person’s sin can bring judgment on the entire community
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:20 recalls Achan’s trespass as causing wrath on all Israel, demonstrating the biblical doctrine that corporate holiness is affected by individual sin.

questions.question: How do the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh defend their altar-building in Joshua 22:24-28?
options: They built it as a witness to prevent future disputes over shared worship rights
They built it to offer independent burnt offerings and sacrifices
They built it to rival the main tabernacle at Shiloh
They built it as an idol to rival the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They built it as a witness to prevent future disputes over shared worship rights
questions.explanation: Verses 24-28 explain the altar was not for offerings but as a witness between the tribes, so their descendants would not dispute their share in the LORD and accuse them of having no part in Him.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by Phinehas’s response upon hearing the tribes’ explanation in Joshua 22:30-31?
options: God’s presence and discernment among His people
God’s wrath and judgment towards sin
God’s silence in human affairs
God’s favoritism towards certain tribes
questions.correctAnswer: God’s presence and discernment among His people
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:31 says Phinehas perceived the LORD was among them because the tribes had not committed trespass, showing God's intimate presence and ability to reveal truth.

questions.question: What is the significance of the altar’s name 'Ed' as given by the children of Reuben and Gad in Joshua 22:34?
options: It signifies a witness that the LORD is God between the tribes
It means 'victory' in the land of Gilead
It commemorates a battle won against Canaan
It refers to a place of sacrifice for idols
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies a witness that the LORD is God between the tribes
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:34 states the altar was called Ed, meaning 'witness,' to testify between the tribes that the LORD is God, emphasizing unity in worship despite geographical separation.

questions.question: How does Joshua 22:4-5 combined with Joshua 22:8 convey a theological teaching about God's provision and covenant faithfulness?
options: God grants rest and land possession, and expects faithful obedience and sharing of spoils
God demands sacrifices without concern for obedience
God’s promises depend on military conquest alone
God only blesses those who remain east of Jordan
questions.correctAnswer: God grants rest and land possession, and expects faithful obedience and sharing of spoils
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 affirm God’s rest and land provision contingent on obedience, while verse 8 commands returning with riches and spoils, showing God’s covenant blessings include both rest and material provision linked to faithfulness.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth about inter-tribal unity and worship does Joshua 22:10 and Joshua 22:24-28 teach?
options: True unity requires mutual recognition and shared worship practices, not separate altars for offerings
Unity is maintained by building competing altars
Worship can be divided geographically without consequence
Altar building is irrelevant to covenant faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: True unity requires mutual recognition and shared worship practices, not separate altars for offerings
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:10’s altar caused suspicion of division, but 22:24-28 clarifies the altar’s purpose was a witness, not for offerings, emphasizing that unity in worship involves mutual recognition without separatist religious acts.

questions.question: What narrative role does the episode of the altar in Joshua 22 play in the broader redemptive history of Israel’s settlement?
options: It highlights the tension and resolution necessary for covenant unity during territorial division
It shows Israel’s immediate failure to obey God’s law
It marks the end of God’s covenant with Israel
It initiates the building of Solomon’s temple
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the tension and resolution necessary for covenant unity during territorial division
questions.explanation: This narrative (Joshua 22) reveals the challenges of maintaining covenant unity when tribes are geographically separated, showing God’s provision for peace and mutual understanding in His redemptive plan.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the altar incident in Joshua 22 demonstrates Israel’s disunity and religious confusion. What does Joshua 22:21-31 actually teach about Israel’s approach to covenant faithfulness?
options: It demonstrates a process of seeking understanding and reconciliation within covenant community
It shows that Israel immediately accepted rebellion without question
It reveals that Israel abandoned the LORD’s commands
It proves that Israelites built multiple altars for idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates a process of seeking understanding and reconciliation within covenant community
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:21-31 shows the tribes explain their intentions clearly and the other leaders discern the truth, leading to peace rather than war, highlighting covenantal dialogue and unity rather than confusion.

questions.question: What doctrinal lesson about sanctification and holiness can be drawn from Joshua 22:19 in relation to land possession and worship?
options: Physical land sanctity affects proper worship and covenant participation
Holiness is irrelevant to geography
Worship can be practiced anywhere without concern for sanctity
Land possession guarantees salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Physical land sanctity affects proper worship and covenant participation
questions.explanation: Joshua 22:19 suggests if the land is unclean, the tribes should join the LORD’s possession where His tabernacle dwells, indicating the role of holy place in worship and covenant identity.
